svg.aria-label: Diagram: Amazon Inspector can now scan EC2 AMIs for software vulnerabilities without launching instances or installing additional software, finding issues at the source before AMIs are used to launch instances across a fleet. Scanning and enforcement are separate mechanisms with different scopes. Inspector scanning can be enabled for an account or across an entire organization. The Allowed AMIs setting turns scan results into a launch rule through a ScanResultCondition, which takes a maximum severity label from informational, low, medium, high and critical, and which blocks AMIs that Amazon Inspector has not scanned. However, the Allowed AMIs feature only controls the discovery and use of public AMIs or AMIs shared with your account and does not restrict the AMIs owned by your account, which remain always discoverable and usable regardless of the criteria set. For AMIs you build yourself the enforcement point is the EC2 Image Builder pipeline, which can restrict distribution of AMIs that do not meet security standards. The diagram also notes that Allowed AMIs gates launches rather than running instances, that audit mode applies the criteria without restricting discoverability or usage, that the settings must be configured in each Region, and that a scan result is true as of a date because a fix can become available for a finding at any time.
svg.title: Inspector tells you; Allowed AMIs stops a launch — but not of your own images
svg.text: The scan is new. The enforcement is an existing control with its own scope.
Inspector AMI scanning — “without launching instances or installing additional software”.
INSPECTOR — tells you
“continuous evaluations to monitor your AMI catalog
for newly discovered vulnerabilities”, or one-time scans.
Enables “for an account or across your entire
organization”. Changes nothing about what can launch.
ALLOWED AMIs — stops a launch
ScanResultCondition
MaximumSeverityLabel: informational … critical
Fails closed: “blocks AMIs that Amazon Inspector
hasn’t scanned”.
The scope the announcement does not mention
“The Allowed AMIs feature only controls the discovery and use of public AMIs or AMIs shared with your
account. It does not restrict the AMIs owned by your account. Regardless of the criteria you set, the AMIs
created by your account are always discoverable and usable by users in your account.”
Which is exactly the AMIs an Image Builder pipeline produces.
AMIs from outside
Public, or shared with your account.
Gate: Allowed AMIs, on the scan result.
This is what the feature is for.
AMIs you build
Owned by your account — never gated by Allowed AMIs.
Gate: the pipeline — “restrict distribution of AMIs that
do not meet their security standards”.
Before you enforce anything
Audit mode: “The ImageCriteria are applied, but no restrictions are placed on AMI discoverability or usage.”
And the gate is launch-time: “Instances can only be launched using allowed AMIs” — nothing stops what runs.
A clean scan is a statement about a date.
“A fix can become available for a finding on an AMI at any time, so an AMI that meets your criteria today
might not meet them after a few days.” The AMI did not change; the world did.
Regional, like the snapshot setting: “configured in each AWS Region where you want to control AMI usage”.
